plays_on: iPhones (App Store) — the build needs a Mac with Xcode
choose.suits: 2D or 3D, with the mobile ecosystem (ads, in-app purchases, device testing); needs the Unity editor and an account, and a build module per place
choose.pick_when: phones are where it is played first, or it needs ads or purchases

editor.name: Unity
missing: Install Unity Hub (https://unity.com/download), sign in and activate the license, then install the editor with Installs → Install Editor — when installing, pick the build module for each place the game is played (Android Build Support with OpenJDK · Android SDK & NDK Tools; iOS Build Support).
If it is installed somewhere else, put the executable's path in the environment variable UNITY and run this again.

modules.name: Android Build Support
install: Close the editor, then Unity Hub → Installs → the gear on that version ({version}) → Add modules → pick Android Build Support together with OpenJDK · Android SDK & NDK Tools.
From a shell: "/Applications/Unity Hub.app/Contents/MacOS/Unity Hub" -- --headless install-modules --version {version} -m android android-sdk-ndk-tools android-open-jdk
It downloads several GB — run it only after the user says to, and wait until it finishes.

modules.name: iOS Build Support
install: Close the editor, then Unity Hub → Installs → the gear on that version ({version}) → Add modules → pick iOS Build Support.
From a shell: "/Applications/Unity Hub.app/Contents/MacOS/Unity Hub" -- --headless install-modules --version {version} -m ios
Building for an iPhone also needs Xcode (Mac App Store) on this Mac. Run the install only after the user says to.
